shape_hint: Thick round washer with a round bore; one face is flat and the other is a convex spherical cap (radius r1) so in section it looks like a plano-convex disc with a low rim of height h1 and a total height h; it sits in a matching concave conical seat (form D) to compensate for angular misalignment.

role_map.d: bore diameter of the spherical washer, minimum = nominal (H13)
role_map.d3: outer diameter of the spherical washer (dc)
role_map.h: total height of the spherical washer (symbol h2 in lexikon/boltsfastener, h in fuller)
role_map.h1: height at the rim of the washer (symbol h1 in all three sources)

notes: Form C = spherical washer (Kugelscheibe), case-hardened; it is paired with form D, the conical seat washer (Kegelpfanne), which is NOT published here (2 sources only; D has d = 7.1, 9.6, 12 ... and d4 = d3). Sizes refer to the bolt (M6..M30); the bore d is larger than the bolt (e.g. M12 -> 13). The boltsfastener.com page appears to be a compiled site (its other tables show label errors), so its independence from the other two cannot be proven; all three tables are identical for the 8 kept rows. DIN 6319 corresponds to no ISO standard according to schrauben-lexikon.

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched fuller (200), schrauben-lexikon DIN_6319C (200), boltsfastener din-6319 (200) and additionally fasteners.eu /standards/DIN/6319/ (200). Parsed all with tbl.py. Matrix 8 rows (M6..M30) x 5 cols (d,d3,h,h1,r1) x 4 sources = 160 comparisons: 160/160 numerically equal, 0 mismatches. fasteners.eu columns d1,d3,h1,h2(C),r1 read by header+sub-header (C/D/G); lexikon mapped to M-sizes via bore d (lexikon has no M labels). Sanity: d3>d, h>h1, all monotone except h1 (M6 0.7 > M8 0.6, present identically in all 4 sources); sagitta of sphere SR over d3 (M6: 9-sqrt(81-36)=2.29) matches h=2.3, so r1 is a radius.
problems: PRODUCER'S 3-CLUSTER CLAIM DOES NOT HOLD AS WRITTEN: boltsfastener.com cannot be counted (compilation site, same symbol set/decimal-comma style as fasteners.eu, also has an M5 row found nowhere else). Without it the producer's sources give only 2 clusters (fuller + lexikon).

Rows survive only because the verifier found a genuine third source: fasteners.eu /standards/DIN/6319/ (Czech portal, own table with d1,d2,d3,d4,d5,f1,h1,h2,h3,r1, thread size, weight, bolting force; different layout from fuller and lexikon; no shared typos). Values for all 8 kept rows x 5 cols equal in fuller, lexikon, fasteners.eu. Publish ONLY if the record's sources list is changed: replace boltsfastener.com by https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/DIN/6319/. If the maintainer refuses to count fasteners.eu, verdict becomes reject (2 clusters).

fasteners.eu legend is sloppy (r1 'diameter of the sphere', h2 'washer width'); r1 role (radius, SR) and h role (total height) are confirmed by fuller (SR, h) and lexikon (r1, h2) instead; fasteners.eu column roles used by header symbol only.
Lexikon table has no thread-size labels (columns are labelled by bore d); M-size label comes from fuller/fasteners.eu ('for thread diameter' / 'Thread size').
h1 non-monotonic (M6 0.7 > M8 0.6) is a real feature of the standard (all 4 sources agree); keep.
